INDUCTOR IDENTIFICATION
OBJECTIVES
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
Nida Experiment Card PC130 - 11
The physical appearance of inductors vary.
INTRODUCTIONM
Inductors are identified by the type of core they have. The most common cores used are air and iron.
Some inductors have their inductor value printed on the body.
Sometimes the value is indicated by the color code used to indicate resistance values. When the henry value is not indicated, you must refer to a schematic.
Let's begin the lesson on INDUCTOR IDENTIFICATION.........................
LESSON MENU
Pick up PC130-11. There are six inductors labeled L1 through L6. They are all iron core inductors.
EXPERIMENT
Values of molded body inductors are printed on them or indicated by a color code.
When using the color code, inductor values are in microhenrys until the multiplier band is applied to the value.
Look at L1. It is a 10 mH inductor. The first band, large silver, indicates that it is an inductor.
The second and third bands indicate significant digits, and the fourth band is the multiplier.
* Note: Orange = 103 or 1000 which equals 10000 mh or 10 mH

When a decimal point is indicated, the 4th band is no longer a multiplier. The 4th band becomes a significant digit.

Molded body inductors that have their values stamped on them are being used more often.
There is no code or multiplier used when the value is stamped on the inductor. The inductors value and tolerance are shown on the inductor.
L3 and L4 are covered with a rubber like coating. This protects the wire in the inductor from shorting out to another component.
Notice that the values are not printed on them and a color code is not used. In this case you must refer to a schematic for the value.
